title: JWT Token Contains Unique Identifier
description: JWT tokens typically contain unique user identifiers that can be used to link data across systems and sessions.
assumptions: JWT tokens are used for authentication and contain user identification information.

title: User Data Contains Quasi-identifiers
description: User data transmitted alongside JWT may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., email, role, department) that can serve as quasi-identifiers for linking.
assumptions: User data includes multiple attributes that could be combined to identify individuals.

title: Processing of Identified Data
description: The flow transmits identified user data (JWT + user data) from authentication service to parent user, processing identifiable information.
assumptions: JWT and user data contain information that identifies the data subject.

title: JWT Contains Unique Identifier Reference
description: JWT tokens contain unique references to the identity of the data subject, enabling identification.
assumptions: JWT tokens are designed to uniquely identify authenticated users.

title: Potentially Sensitive User Data Collected
description: User data transmitted may include sensitive information beyond what is strictly required for authentication purposes.
assumptions: User data may contain more sensitive attributes than needed for the authentication service functionality.

title: Data Propagation to Parent User
description: User data is propagated from authentication service to parent user, potentially exposing data to parties where it may not be needed.
assumptions: Parent user may not require all user data transmitted in the JWT.

title: Parent User Unaware of Data Processing
description: Parent user may not be fully aware of the collection and processing of their personal data through the authentication service.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into what data is transmitted and how it's used.

title: Lack of User Control Over Data Processing
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their personal data is processed in the authentication flow.
assumptions: Authentication service may not provide granular consent options for data processing.

title: Potential Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: User data transmitted may exceed what is actually needed for authentication functionality, potentially violating data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR and similar regulations require data minimization in authentication processes.

title: Linking through parent email identifier
description: Parent email serves as a unique identifier that can link the child's login activity to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the child's usage patterns to the parent or third parties.
assumptions: Email addresses are typically unique identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combination through email and password
description: The combination of parent email and password can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow linking of login sessions to specific individuals.
assumptions: Email+password combination may be unique enough for identification

title: Processing of identified data during child login
description: The authentication service processes identified personal data (parent email and password) during the child login process, which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Email and password are clearly identifiable personal data

title: Email as unique identifier for data subject
description: Parent email contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (parent), which is processed during child authentication.
assumptions: Email addresses are unique identifiers

title: Collection of highly sensitive password data
description: Password is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required. The system collects and processes password data during authentication.
assumptions: Passwords are among the most sensitive personal data types

title: Unnecessary processing of password data
description: Password data is processed for authentication purposes, but the extent of processing (storage, hashing, etc.) may exceed what is functionally needed for the login functionality.
assumptions: Password processing may include unnecessary transformations

title: Child unawareness of data processing implications
description: The child user may not be fully aware of the implications of using parent credentials for their own login, including data collection and processing.
assumptions: Children may lack understanding of privacy implications

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The child user has limited control over how their parent's data is processed, stored, and potentially shared during the authentication process.
assumptions: Children typically have limited privacy controls

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing parent email and password for child login may process more personal data than functionally necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle requires processing only necessary data

title: Potential invalid consent for child data processing
description: Children may not provide valid consent for processing their parent's personal data, raising questions about lawfulness of the processing activity.
assumptions: Children's consent may not be legally valid under GDPR

title: Linking through JWT identifier
description: The JWT token contains unique identifiers that can be used to link data across systems and sessions, potentially enabling tracking of the child user across different authentication contexts.

title: Linking through child profile quasi-identifiers
description: Child profiles may contain combinations of attributes (age, location, interests) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling linking of data across different sources when combined with other information.

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The authentication service processes identified child data through JWT tokens and child profiles, which contain personal information that directly identifies the child user.

title: Identifier in JWT token
description: The JWT token contains unique references to the identity of the child data subject, enabling direct identification through the authentication mechanism.

title: Excessive data type sensitivity
description: Child profiles may contain more sensitive personal data than functionally required for authentication purposes, including potentially sensitive information about the child's characteristics.

title: Excessive volume of child data
description: The volume of child profile data being transmitted may exceed what is functionally needed for the authentication service to operate.

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: As a child user, the data subject may not fully understand the implications of their personal data being collected, processed, and transmitted through the authentication service.

title: Lack of child control over data preferences
description: Children may lack the capacity to set meaningful preferences or provide valid consent regarding how their personal data is processed and stored.

title: GDPR violation of data minimization
description: Processing child data may violate GDPR data minimization principles if more personal data is collected and processed than is actually needed for the authentication functionality.

title: Invalid consent for child data processing
description: Children may not be able to provide valid consent for data processing, and parental consent mechanisms may be insufficient or improperly implemented.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video content is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for streaming approved video to a child.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: Video data may be captured at a finer granularity than necessary, potentially revealing more personal details than required for the streaming functionality.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is needed to achieve the streaming functionality to the child.

title: Excessive party exposure
description: Video data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, increasing exposure risk.

title: Revealing attributes in video
description: Video content may contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject (child or individuals in the video).

title: Small anonymity set
description: Video content may allow singling out an individual data subject due to small anonymity set (e.g., unique location, time, or context).

title: Quasi-identifier combination in video
description: Video content may contain combinations of attributes (location, time, activity) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals.

title: Individual profiling through video
description: Video data may be analyzed for patterns to link data to specific individuals or infer personal characteristics.

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: The child data subject may not be aware of the collection, processing, or storage of their video data.

title: Lack of consent preferences
description: The child may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed.

title: Lack of rectification/erasure control
description: The child may lack control to rectify incorrect video data or remove video data that is no longer relevant.

title: GDPR data minimization violation
description: Video data may be processed in excess of what is actually needed, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.

title: Invalid consent for child data
description: Video data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent, particularly concerning child data subjects who require parental consent.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in browsing data
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, cookies, user IDs) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across systems.
assumptions: Browsing data collection includes identifier tracking mechanisms

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Browsing data contains multiple quasi-identifiers (IP address, device type, browsing patterns, timestamps) that when combined can uniquely identify individuals.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to sufficient quasi-identifiers to perform re-identification

title: Profiling an individual through browsing behavior
description: Advertisers can analyze browsing data patterns to build profiles of individuals, linking behavioral data to specific users for targeted advertising.
assumptions: Advertisers employ profiling algorithms on received browsing data

title: Processing of identifiable information
description: Browsing data may contain direct identifiers or unique references that allow identification of data subjects when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Browsing data collection includes user identification mechanisms

title: Revealing attributes in browsing data
description: Browsing data reveals sensitive attributes about users including interests, preferences, location patterns, and behavioral characteristics that support identification.
assumptions: Browsing data includes detailed behavioral and contextual information

title: Data propagation to third-party advertisers
description: Browsing data is propagated from the AI Recommendation Engine to external third-party advertisers beyond what may be functionally necessary for the core recommendation functionality.
assumptions: Data sharing with advertisers is not strictly required for the primary AI recommendation function

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Browsing data is made accessible to a predetermined set of third-party advertisers, expanding exposure beyond the immediate system boundary.
assumptions: Advertiser relationships are established and fixed at design time

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected and shared with third-party advertisers for advertising purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate data sharing with advertisers

title: Lack of control over data sharing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack meaningful control over how their browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers, including inability to opt-out or customize sharing preferences.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms for third-party data sharing may be unclear or difficult to exercise

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Browsing data shared with advertisers may exceed what is functionally necessary for the stated purpose, potentially including more detailed or extensive data than required.
assumptions: Data sharing agreements may not enforce strict minimization requirements

title: Potential invalid consent for data sharing
description: Consent for sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may not be valid due to lack of clear information, granular consent options, or meaningful user choice.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not meet regulatory standards for validity

title: Processing of identified data
description: The Authentication Service processes government ID images which are clearly identified personal data that directly identifies individuals.

title: Identifier in data
description: Government ID images contain unique identifiers that directly reference the identity of the data subject.

title: Revealing attributes
description: ID images reveal biometric and other identifying attributes that support identification of the data subject.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required.

title: Duration/retention
description: Unclear how long government ID images are retained in the file system, potentially exceeding functional necessity.

title: Involved parties
description: Personal data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary in the backend file system.

title: Unawareness as data subject
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their government ID images are being stored in the file system.

title: Preferences
description: Data subjects lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their ID images are processed and stored.

title: Access
description: Data subjects may lack control in accessing the personal data that is being processed and stored.

title: Rectification/erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control in rectifying incorrect data or removing personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Government ID images may represent more personal data than is actually needed for the authentication service functionality.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Personal data may be stored longer than needed without clear retention policies.

title: JWT contains unique identifier
description: JWT tokens contain unique references to user identity (user ID, session ID, etc.) that can directly identify the data subject.
assumptions: JWT tokens are issued with unique identifiers that can be used to identify specific users.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The authentication service processes identified data (JWT) that contains personal information about the user.
assumptions: JWT tokens are processed by the authentication service for authentication purposes.

title: Sensitive authentication data stored in localStorage
description: JWT tokens contain sensitive authentication credentials that should be stored with higher security than localStorage provides.
assumptions: JWT tokens are considered sensitive authentication data that requires secure storage.

title: JWT retention may exceed functional need
description: JWT tokens may be stored in localStorage longer than functionally necessary, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: JWT tokens have expiration times but localStorage may retain them beyond their validity period.

title: User unawareness of JWT storage
description: Users may not be aware that their authentication tokens are being stored in browser localStorage.
assumptions: Users are not informed about the storage of JWT tokens in localStorage.

title: Lack of user control over JWT storage
description: Users have limited control over how JWT tokens are stored in localStorage and cannot easily manage this storage.
assumptions: Browser localStorage provides limited user control mechanisms for managing stored tokens.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing JWT tokens in localStorage may process more data than strictly necessary for authentication functionality.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle requires processing only necessary personal data.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in child history
description: Child history data likely contains unique identifiers (e.g., child ID, birth date, medical record numbers) that can be used to link data across systems or contexts.
assumptions: Child history contains identifiable information that can be used for linking purposes.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in child history
description: Child history may contain multiple quasi-identifiers (e.g., age, location, medical conditions) that when combined can uniquely identify the child even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that can be combined to identify individuals.

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The system processes child history which is identified personal data about the child, not just the parent.
assumptions: Child history contains personal data that identifies the child as a data subject.

title: Revealing attributes in child history
description: Child history contains revealing attributes such as medical conditions, developmental milestones, or behavioral data that can support identification of the child.
assumptions: Child history includes sensitive attributes that reveal personal information about the child.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Child history is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for parent review functionality.
assumptions: Child history contains sensitive medical or developmental data that may be more sensitive than required.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and enrichment
description: Child history data may be further analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is needed for simple parent review.
assumptions: The system may process child history data in ways that go beyond basic retrieval and display.

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their history is being retrieved and reviewed by the parent through this system.
assumptions: Children typically lack awareness of data processing activities involving their personal information.

title: Lack of child control over data processing
description: The child has no control over how their history data is collected, processed, or shared with the parent.
assumptions: Children cannot provide meaningful consent or control over their data processing.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing child history may violate data minimization by collecting and processing more personal data than necessary for the parent review functionality.
assumptions: GDPR and similar regulations require data minimization, and child history may contain excessive data.
